items.headline: Eight public officers referred to police over home buys near unannounced MRT stations
items.summary: Coordinating Minister for Public Services Chan Chun Sing told Parliament on 6 October that eight public officers involved in rail planning have been referred to the police after a review of property purchases near MRT stations whose sites had not yet been announced; he said transactions involving 191 officers had been checked so far and that a referral does not mean wrongdoing has been established.

items.headline: LTA to prioritise North-South Corridor surface works to cut noise and dust by end-2027
items.summary: Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow told Parliament on 6 October that the Land Transport Authority will prioritise surface works on the delayed North-South Corridor to reduce noise and dust by the end of 2027, explaining that the route passes through densely built-up areas and must bypass major utilities, heavily used roads and existing MRT lines.

items.headline: Driver jailed 12 years and nine months over 2024 Tampines collision that killed two
items.summary: A 45-year-old driver was sentenced to 12 years and nine months’ jail and disqualified from driving for life over a chain collision in Tampines on 24 April 2024 that killed two people and injured others.

items.headline: High Court dismisses S$1.7 million claim over a late businessman’s gifts to a woman
items.summary: A Singapore court dismissed a suit by a late businessman’s daughter seeking to recover more than S$1.7 million transferred to a 39-year-old woman, finding the money had been given voluntarily, and ordered the estate to pay the woman S$209,856 in legal costs.

items.headline: Update: Rahul Gandhi detained as voter-roll protests escalate across India
items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was briefly detained in New Delhi on 6 October as a 20-party opposition alliance marched to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar; protesters say a nationwide voter-roll revision has struck more than 130 million names, hitting the poor and minorities hardest, to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP.

items.headline: Update: RBI poised for its first interest-rate rise in nearly four years
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to announce its first rate increase in almost four years when its monetary policy committee concludes on 7 October, with a rupee near record lows and an oil-price spike pushing Governor Sanjay Malhotra toward a quarter-point rise to 5.50%; it would be the first hike of his tenure after a run of cuts.

items.headline: Update: India-US trade talks stall as a 100% tariff on Russian-oil buyers looms
items.summary: Top US and Indian officials signalled that negotiations over a trade deal have reached an impasse, days after Washington enacted a law allowing tariffs of up to 100% on countries that buy Russian oil — a measure due to take effect within weeks that New Delhi has described as a ‘deal breaker’ in the relationship.

items.headline: India’s Gen-Z ‘cockroach’ movement puts Modi on the defensive
items.summary: A youth-led protest movement that embraced the ‘cockroach’ label has spread from campuses to the streets of Mumbai and Delhi, merging with the voter-roll anger into what commentators call the broadest challenge to Modi in years; the government has ringed Parliament and the Election Commission with heavy security.

items.headline: Badenoch pledges to abolish inheritance tax and expand childcare in a middle-class pitch
items.summary: At the Conservative conference, leader Kemi Badenoch promised to abolish inheritance tax and widen childcare support to higher earners, a pitch aimed at aspirational voters drifting to Nigel Farage’s Reform UK, which has narrowed Labour’s lead under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

items.headline: Badenoch names Andrew Griffith shadow chancellor to sharpen the Tory economic attack
items.summary: Kemi Badenoch appointed Andrew Griffith as shadow chancellor to lead the opposition’s economic case against Burnham’s Labour government, pressing questions over how ministers will fund their commitments as UK government borrowing climbs.

items.headline: Burnham’s ‘Manchesterism’ economic vision faces an uphill battle
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s plan to break with the Thatcher era — promising greater public control of key utilities and more regional power — is running into fiscal reality, with analysts questioning how it can be funded amid a severe cost-of-living squeeze and rising borrowing.

items.headline: Former Prince Andrew’s bid to quash Windsor search warrants heads to the High Court
items.summary: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s judicial review seeking to quash the warrants Thames Valley Police used to search his former Windsor home is due before the High Court this week; he was arrested earlier this year on suspicion of misconduct in public office over claims he passed information to Jeffrey Epstein.

items.headline: Israel and Hamas agree the first phase of Trump’s Gaza ceasefire plan
items.summary: Israel and Hamas agreed the first phase of a US-brokered ceasefire built on President Donald Trump’s 20-point plan, providing for a halt in fighting, an Israeli pull-back to an agreed line and an exchange of all remaining hostages for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners.

items.headline: First hostages freed as Trump heads to the Knesset and an Egypt peace summit
items.summary: The first Israeli hostages were released under the deal, with the rest expected within days, as Trump prepared to address the Knesset and then travel to Egypt for a summit of some 20 leaders to launch an international ‘Board of Peace’ to oversee Gaza’s recovery.

items.headline: France hit by its biggest student protests in decades as the PM suspends classes
items.summary: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu suspended high-school classes for the rest of the week as hundreds of thousands protested nationwide over teacher shortages and school conditions; the interior ministry said 6,100 people, most of them minors, had been arrested since the movement began on 21 September.

items.headline: Update: Saudi-led coalition confirms its first Yemen air strikes since the 2022 truce
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said about 100 fighter jets were supporting a more organised government offensive against the Houthis and acknowledged resuming air strikes for the first time since the 2022 truce, as pro-government forces pressed toward the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

items.headline: Reflection AI debuts Beam, an open-weight model to rival China’s at lower cost
items.summary: Brooklyn-based Reflection AI unveiled Beam, its first frontier open-weight model, claiming it matches leading Chinese open models on reasoning benchmarks at far lower compute cost; the startup, founded by two former Google DeepMind researchers, has raised about $4.7 billion from backers including Nvidia and Sequoia.

items.headline: DeepSeek weighs doubling its funding round to as much as $15 billion
items.summary: Chinese AI developer DeepSeek is considering roughly doubling its latest funding round to as much as 100 billion yuan (about $14.9 billion), according to people familiar with the talks, as the race to bankroll frontier models intensifies.

items.headline: A 19-year-old raises $11 million for Ghost, a $3,499 computer for personal AI
items.summary: Personal-AI startup Ghost emerged from stealth with an $11 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz; its first product, Core, is a $3,499 computer designed specifically to run AI agents on a user’s own hardware.

items.headline: Nokia chief says AI data centres would be built twice as fast without chip shortages
items.summary: Nokia’s chief executive said component shortages, not demand, are the main brake on the AI build-out, arguing data centres could be stood up roughly twice as fast if supply bottlenecks for chips and networking gear eased.

items.headline: Saia unveils a chip that runs AI out of flash storage to cut power and cost
items.summary: Among startups showcased at the latest PearX demo day, Saia said it has designed a chip that bypasses conventional memory by running AI models directly from flash storage, claiming eight times the capacity and four times less power than Nvidia’s Jetson.

items.headline: S&P 500 and Nasdaq close at fresh records as oil and yields ease
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to a record 7,818.93 on 6 October and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.45% to a record 27,599.79, led by technology names, while the Dow gained 0.49% to 51,521.28 as oil prices and Treasury yields slipped.

items.headline: Gold climbs toward records as bets on an October Fed rate rise fade
items.summary: Spot gold edged up to about $4,150 an ounce as traders trimmed expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase this month, offsetting a firmer dollar and elevated Treasury yields.

items.headline: Oil steadies with Brent near $101 and WTI near $89
items.summary: Crude prices ended little changed, with Brent settling 0.26% higher at $100.58 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate at $89.44, as the market weighed Middle East diplomacy against OPEC+ supply decisions.

items.headline: Traders await Fed minutes after weak September jobs trim October hike odds
items.summary: Markets pared bets on a Federal Reserve rate increase this month to about 21% after soft September payrolls and downward revisions, while still pricing a near-70% chance of a hike by December, with minutes from the Fed’s September meeting due on 7 October.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell to start the Singapore GP from the back after a Bahrain engine failure
items.summary: Mercedes’ George Russell is set to start this weekend’s Singapore Grand Prix from the back of the grid after a power-unit failure in the rain-hit Bahrain round forced a new engine beyond his season allocation; Marina Bay hosts its first Sprint, with Kimi Antonelli leading the drivers’ championship.

items.headline: 🎾 Update: Djokovic wins a record seventh China Open as de Minaur retires
items.summary: Novak Djokovic won a record-extending seventh China Open title when Alex de Minaur retired with a groin problem after losing the opening set 7-6(3); it was Djokovic’s 102nd tour-level title, one behind Roger Federer’s 103 for second-most in the Open Era.

items.headline: 🎾 Shanghai Masters draw sends Zverev and Djokovic into the same half
items.summary: The Rolex Shanghai Masters draw placed top seed Alexander Zverev and four-time champion Novak Djokovic in the same half, while Carlos Alcaraz opens against Juan Manuel Cerundolo or a qualifier; world No. 1 Jannik Sinner is absent with a knee problem.

items.headline: 🏏 South Africa and Australia open a three-Test series in Durban
items.summary: World Test Championship holders South Africa begin a three-match Test series against Australia at Kingsmead in Durban on 9 October, the countries’ first Test tour since the 2018 ‘sandpaper-gate’ affair, after South Africa took the preceding ODI series 2-1.

items.headline: Francis Halzen wins the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for neutrino astronomy
items.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin-Madison for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, the cubic-kilometre detector buried in Antarctic ice whose capture of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a new window on the cosmos.

items.headline: Brain organoids grafted into mice open a new window on the human cortex
items.summary: Researchers reported that lab-grown human brain organoids transplanted into the brains of mice lacking a cortex mature into neurons that cannot be studied in a dish, a step that could help link brain injury and disease to behaviour.

items.headline: A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer’s genetic weak points
items.summary: Scientists built a large biobank of patient tumour-derived organoids and used it to chart the genes cancers depend on to survive, a resource meant to speed the search for drug targets across many tumour types.

items.headline: Webb spots an exoplanet whose atmosphere defies current theories
items.summary: Astronomers using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reported a planet with an unusual helium- and carbon-dominated atmosphere that standard formation models struggle to explain, deepening questions about how such worlds take shape.

fun_fact.headline: Carrots were not always orange
fun_fact.body: Carrots were not always orange. For most of their history, cultivated carrots were purple, white or yellow, and scholars doubt the orange carrot even existed before the 16th century. Dutch growers selectively bred the sweeter orange variety — the first mention of the ‘long orange Dutch’ carrot dates to 1721 — and its colour comes from beta-carotene, the pigment the body converts into vitamin A.
fun_fact.source: Encyclopedic / primary sources (Britannica, BBC Science Focus, The Economist)

puzzle.title: Ages Across the Street
puzzle.body:
A pollster knocks on a door. A resident says she has three children.

‘The product of their ages is 36,’ she says, ‘and their ages add up to the number on the house across the street.’

The pollster looks at that house number, thinks, and says, ‘That’s still not enough information.’

The resident replies, ‘Oh — my eldest is learning the violin.’ The pollster immediately knows all three ages. What are they?
puzzle.approach: List every trio of whole-number ages whose product is 36, then ask which total would leave the pollster still stuck.
puzzle.answer:
2, 2 and 9.

The trios of whole-number ages with product 36 and their sums are:
(1,1,36) = 38
(1,2,18) = 21
(1,3,12) = 16
(1,4,9) = 14
(1,6,6) = 13
(2,2,9) = 13
(2,3,6) = 11
(3,3,4) = 10

Only the sum 13 is shared by two trios — (1,6,6) and (2,2,9) — so seeing the house number 13 leaves the pollster unable to decide. The clue that there is a single ‘eldest’ child rules out (1,6,6), which has two six-year-olds, leaving 2, 2 and 9.

word_puzzle.title: The Center Holds
word_puzzle.body:
Centre letter: T
Outer letters: A · C · E · N · O · R

Make as many words of four or more letters as you can. Every word must include the centre letter T. There is at least one pangram that uses all seven letters.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must contain the centre letter T and use only the seven letters shown; letters may repeat. Find the pangram that uses all seven.
word_puzzle.answer:
Pangram: CAROTENE (uses A, C, E, N, O, R and T).

Other valid words include:
ACTOR · ORATE · CARET · CATER · CRATE · TRACE · REACT · ENACT · TENOR · TONER · CANTO · CANTER · CARTON · NECTAR · RECANT · TRANCE · CORNET · CARROT · REACTOR · TRACTOR · OCTANE

Every word contains T and uses only the letters A, C, E, N, O, R, T.
